title: Eighth stale-suite triage draw: 50 untriaged unrun test files across ten directories, each executed on its own, and the nine directories that came back clean wired into CI

scope.drawnFrom: governedRiskRanking from scripts/quality/test-ci-coverage-census.mjs, re-derived on this base rather than read from the committed snapshot
scope.ranksMovedUnderTheFiling: The item names ranks 19-28. On this base the same ten directories are ranks 14-23. Nothing about them changed: T-492 wired five directories out of the untriaged set roughly an hour before this draw, and every row below it moved up five places. The DIRECTORY SET and the per-directory count (5 each, 50 total) reproduce the filing exactly, which is why the filing naming them individually rather than by rank is what made the draw survive its own staleness. Both rank numbers are recorded per row -- governedRiskRankAsFiled and governedRiskRankOnThisBase -- so a reader can see the drift rather than take this sentence for it.
scope.censusDriftAtThisBase: The committed census artifact matched a fresh run on this base before any edit in this change, so the draw is reproducible from the census rather than asserted. All ten rows: band unclassified, score 0, admittedBy untriaged_unrun_work, 5 untriaged unrun files each.
scope.nonTestsDirectories: One of the ten is NOT a __tests__ directory: src/lib/intelligence/ask/retrievers holds its five test files beside their sources. The filing warned that a __tests__-shaped glob would silently miss it, and the wiring control asserts the five FILES are selected rather than asserting the directory name appears in a workflow.
scope.disjointnessIsAsserted: src/__tests__/behaviors/t493-stale-suite-triage-record.test.ts reads every sibling stale-suite record and fails if any path appears in two. The filing names five to reconcile against; this reconciles against all eight stale-suite records plus the three non-stale triage records under docs/architecture by exact path, and 0 of the 50 appeared in any of them.

jestEvidence.how: Each of the 50 was executed on its own with `npx jest --runTestsByPath <path> --no-coverage --ci --json --outputFile`, and every count in suites[] is read out of that run's JSON by script rather than typed. --runTestsByPath for all 50 so that no path is read as a regex.
jestEvidence.executedAt: 2026-09-27T13:00:07Z to 2026-09-27T13:00:47Z, before any verdict in this record was written
jestEvidence.harnessFoundTests: Asserted rather than assumed: all 50 runs report numTotalTestSuites === 1 and numTotalTests > 0. A harness that silently matches nothing exits green, which is the failure mode this line exists to exclude.
jestEvidence.alsoRunTogether: The nine wired directories were also run as ONE jest invocation in the shape of the workflow steps: 46 suites / 374 tests / 0 failing. 46 and not 45 because src/scripts/__tests__ also holds the already-owned worker-boundary suite. 373 of those cases are this draw's 45 wired files and the 374th is that suite's single case, which is the cross-check that the per-file numbers and the directory run describe the same population.

caseAttribution.whyPublishedRatherThanGuessed: Byte-matching cases are attributed by locating read calls inside a case body, which needs the static case openers to account for every runtime case. One suite in this draw, structured-exhibits.test.ts, generates cases rather than writing them out: 38 static openers against 45 runtime cases. For that suite the attribution has no denominator, so it is published as unattributable instead of being filled in with a number a later reader would treat as measured.

classifierCorrection.whatTheFirstPassReported: The first mechanical pass bound identifiers assigned from readFileSync by NAME and then counted any case body containing that token. It reported 32 of 43 cases in run-migrations.test.ts as byte-matching.
classifierCorrection.whyItWasWrong: The identifier was `sql`, which appears in 32 case bodies of a suite about a SQL migration runner with nothing to do with reading a file. A name-based signal cannot see scope, and 32 of 43 would have made that suite look like a scanner.
classifierCorrection.whatTheSecondPassAsks: Whether a case body contains a read call whose own argument expression is anchored to the repository root (process.cwd(), __dirname, or a literal repo-relative path) and not to a temporary directory. That question a regex can answer. It reports exactly 1 repo-anchored read in each of the three suites that have one, and 1 byte-matching case each.
classifierCorrection.theLimitOfTheInstrument: Comments are stripped before scanning, because `// simulates readFileSync throwing ENOENT` is a sentence about a call rather than a call. Stripping is itself approximate -- a `//` inside a string literal would be cut too -- and no row in this draw depends on that edge.

wiring.namedAsDirectories: Each of the nine is named as a DIRECTORY, without a trailing slash, for the two reasons in that workflow's header: a trailing slash stops the coverage gate matching, and file-by-file wiring is the shape of the defect. A suite added to any of the nine tomorrow runs the day it lands.
wiring.provenBy: src/__tests__/behaviors/t493-wired-directory-ci-coverage.test.ts, which answers through the census's own resolver rather than by grepping the workflow for a string, asserts the retrievers directory's five FILES resolve rather than its name appearing, and refuses a re-add to the dark baseline.
wiring.nineOfTenOnly: Nine of the ten drawn directories are wired. The tenth, src/lib/intelligence/synthesis/__tests__, holds both deferred rows -- one red suite and one source-text scanner -- and a directory is wired by fixing it, never by adding it to a green command. Its three green siblings stay dark until those two are settled, which is the cost of that rule and is stated rather than hidden.
wiring.darkBaselineMovement: Eight lines leave src/__tests__/behaviors/product-directory-ci-coverage.baseline.json, not nine, and the difference is measured rather than reasoned: two census runs on this base, before and after the workflow edit, show exactly those eight leaving the uncovered set with nothing entering it, while src/scripts/__tests__ was 5 of 6 covered and therefore PARTIAL, so wiring it moved it out of the partial set and never reached the dark one.
wiring.deliberateOverlap: src/scripts/__tests__ re-runs one suite a pinned step already owns. Measured: that suite alone is 1 case in 0.858s because it spawns a node subprocess to check import conditions, against 1.111s for the whole six-suite directory. The pinned step is left in place rather than removed, because it is named in another item's record and renaming another item's check is a widening this change does not need.

heldDirectories.src/lib/intelligence/synthesis/__tests__: Held on ONE surviving leg, down from two. The hold stands, and all five files stay unrun. violationsMigration.test.ts is a source-text scanner over a committed migration that T-550's rule refuses to wire, whether it passes or not -- owner T-495, verdict rewrite_as_behavior, and that is now the whole of the reason. The other leg expired on 2026-09-27: violationsSupabaseBackend.test.ts was red on a mock aimed at a seam its subject no longer uses, and item T-497 repaired it (PR #8574) -- the mock now sits on the Azure/Postgres seam the subject actually calls, 3 of 4 cases red before and 0 of 4 after. T-497 did NOT wire it, because this hold is asserted by a control at directory granularity and covers every file here. Three green siblings -- healthcareAnswerContract, outputValidator and violationsRecorder, 36 cases between them -- plus the now-green violationsSupabaseBackend stay dark as a result, so four of the five are blocked solely on the fifth. 10 non-test files import this tree. This reason was rewritten rather than left standing because a hold whose stated basis has half expired reads as more blocked than it is. UPDATE 2026-10-01 (item 26): the hold now covers the directory NAME and the scanner only. The four green siblings -- healthcareAnswerContract, outputValidator, violationsRecorder and violationsSupabaseBackend, 40 cases on base 35b8b3e7dd, each subject imported by product code -- run by NAMED FILE in .github/workflows/unit-suites.yml (see namedFileWiring). violationsMigration.test.ts stays unrun until T-495 settles its lane.

namedFileWiring.step: Run the T-493 held synthesis suites by named file
namedFileWiring.why: The suite rows keep wiredInThisItem false: T-493 did not wire them, and its record is history. This block is the later change. A directory holding a declared scanner is never named whole; its green, reachable siblings are named by file, the shape T-780 established.

drawConcentration.whyItMatters: This draw is perfectly flat: all ten directories hold exactly 5 files, so there is no dominant directory and the reported dominant one is simply the first in path order. That is the opposite of T-492, where one directory held 23 of 84, and it is the reason the filing said the order among these ten is path order and nothing else. A reader should not infer that the first row is the riskiest; the ranking cannot distinguish them at all, and every one of the ten is band unclassified with score 0, which is a recorded absence of signal rather than a finding of low risk.

vacuousControlsDeclared.sourceTextScanner: PARTLY VACUOUS, and said so rather than dressed up: 3 of the 50 read repository file text and 1 carries sourceTextScanner true. The refusing half of the control fired once, on the one migration scanner, and the control that makes a text-reading row argue its way out fired twice. What it did NOT do is separate a large population: 47 of the 50 read no repository file at all, so the rule is cheap here and its value is that the three exceptions are named rather than swept into the wiring.
vacuousControlsDeclared.redSuites: NOT VACUOUS. 1 of the 50 is red -- 3 failing cases -- and it carries a verdict that does not assume it passes. In the merged history its subject and itself arrive in the same squash with the subject already on the Azure client, so it has never passed and no workflow ran it to say so.
vacuousControlsDeclared.partialSourceTextCases: NOT VACUOUS. 2 rows carry partialSourceTextCases above zero, so the control naming every byte-matching case inside a non-scanner suite fired rather than passing over an empty set. Both are 1 case of 14 and 1 of 43: calling either suite a scanner would have barred thirteen tenant-fence assertions and forty-two runner assertions from CI.
vacuousControlsDeclared.caseAttribution: NOT VACUOUS in the direction that matters: 1 of the 50 cannot be attributed case by case and the record names it, so the guard asserts a published limit rather than an empty one.

forbiddenEdits: This record judges 50 files and edits none of them. The guard asserts claimedWriteFiles and the judged paths are disjoint, which is what keeps a triage from quietly repairing its own subject and reporting the repair as a finding.

followOnItems.T-495: Owns the 14 source-text scanners from the T-492 draw and gains a 15th here: src/lib/intelligence/synthesis/__tests__/violationsMigration.test.ts, whose single case asserts seven substrings of a committed migration including that row-level security is enabled and the read grant is tenant-scoped. WHICH HALF OF T-495 IT FALLS IN IS NOT THIS RECORD'S TO DECIDE, and the honest answer is that the two readings disagree. T-495's gate scope names THREE SPECIFIC ROWS, the ones carrying textIsTheSubject, and this is not one of them -- this row carries textIsTheSubject false, because whether a table has row-level security is executable against a database and parseable from the SQL, so text is not the only subject available. By the letter of that split the row is in T-495's claimable half. By its nature it needs the same lane decision the gated half exists for: there is no module to execute here, so 'rewrite against what the module returns' has no target, and the real choice is between a governance validator over migrations and a parsed model of the DDL. Whoever takes T-495 should read that disagreement rather than inherit a verdict from this record.
followOnItems.T-497: Owns the four suites that execute real code and disagree with it, and gains a fifth here: src/lib/intelligence/synthesis/__tests__/violationsSupabaseBackend.test.ts. Its acceptance already prescribes what this row needs -- decide whether the code or the expectation is right and say which, citing the commit that moved it. The answer is recorded in this row's rationale: the product is right, the expectation has to move to the seam the module actually uses, and the commit is 5d795a3976.

unfiledSuccessor.whatIsOwed: A wiring item for src/lib/intelligence/synthesis/__tests__, to be taken once T-495 and T-497 clear its two deferred rows. Its three green siblings -- healthcareAnswerContract, outputValidator and violationsRecorder, 36 cases -- stay dark until then.
unfiledSuccessor.whyItIsNotFiled: Both T-lane id bands an agent may draw from report 0 of 100 free on this base: T-500 to T-599 for Claude Code and T-400 to T-499 for a human. The execution queue prints that as a range decision rather than a reading, and it has now blocked a filing in two separate runs on 2026-09-27. Taking the next number anyway is the collision the band rule exists to prevent, and taking one from another actor's band is the same defect with a different owner.
unfiledSuccessor.howItIsKeptVisible: The three rows carry ownerItem null with an ownerItemUnfiled block, the guard refuses that branch unless this section exists, and the backlog entry for T-493 repeats it. Nothing here reads as finished.

7 cases over the gate predicates the section above consumes: provider certification, missing-versus-zero, and uncertified-versus-clean. The distinction this asserts is the one the render gate exists for.
3 cases mounting the Knowledge shell. A smoke suite is thin evidence on its own and cheap to keep; it catches a shell that stops rendering at all, which is the failure a page-level change produces.
3 cases asserting that the Knowledge components a route mounts are the ones that exist. This is the orphaned-component class the repository has paid for repeatedly.
5 cases driving the gate and the section together, so the composed behaviour is covered and not only the two halves.
4 cases over claim-source validation in the aVa answer path. 60 non-test files import this tree, so it is coverage over code that runs on a live answer.
5 cases over the composer itself, the function every aVa answer passes through.
6 cases over the CXO quality gate, which decides whether an answer is fit to show an executive. A gate nothing runs is the defect this whole item family exists to remove.
16 cases over the public-answer scrub — the control that keeps restricted content out of a public-facing answer. The largest suite in this directory and the one whose silence would cost most.
2 cases over the render-layer shaper. Thin, green, and cheap to own.
6 cases over answer safety in the Intelligence answer path, 11 importers outside the tree.
4 cases pinning a reproduced leak of follow-up text into an answer. A reproduction suite that nothing runs cannot report the regression it was written for.
4 cases over the answer router's intent dispatch.

45 cases over structured exhibits, the largest suite in the draw's Intelligence half. Its cases are generated rather than statically written, so this record cannot attribute them one by one and says so rather than filling the column in.
12 cases over the streaming fence filter, which decides what a user sees mid-stream. Streaming defects are invisible to a suite nothing runs.

suites.rationale: Its one case reads a committed SQL migration and asserts seven substrings of it, including that row-level security is enabled and the read grant is tenant-scoped. suites.rationale: RED: 3 of 4 cases fail. The suite mocks @/lib/supabase-server's getServerSupabase, and its subject does not call it — violationsSupabaseBackend.ts imports getAzureWriteFluentClient from @/lib/data-plane/postgresCompat, so the mock intercepts nothing and the real client asks for a database URL that is absent in unit CI: `Missing ABARVA_AZURE_DATABASE_URL or DATABASE_URL`. The product is the half that is right — AGENTS.md requires the Azure/Postgres data-plane adapters and forbids new direct Supabase clients — so the expectation is what has to move, to the seam the module actually uses. In the merged history both files arrive in the same squash, 5d795a3976, with the module already on the Azure client, so this suite has never passed and nothing could report it: the directory is run by no workflow. This record does not edit it; the guard forbids editing a file it judges, and the item that owns suites which execute real code and disagree with it is T-497.
suites.deferredReason: Red, and this record may not edit a file it judges. T-497 owns suites that execute real code and disagree with it.

byteMatchingCaseNames: requires a non-null approved version before criterion approval can pass
suites.rationale: 14 cases over the scorecard authority store, and it is the suite this draw had to argue about. Thirteen cases drive the store against a mocked client and assert governed refusals: an opposite-tenant row is refused even when the query returns it, a score belonging to another event is refused, and absent authority is distinguished from an unapplied schema. One case reads the committed migration and asserts a non-null approved version is required before criterion approval. Calling the whole suite a scanner on the strength of that one case would bar thirteen tenant-fence assertions from CI, which is the opposite of what the scanner rule protects.
